title: Computing 2000–2009
tagline: Broadband, mobile and the cloud begin.
source: Generated from “Timeline of computing 2000–2009” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: Nokia announces the Nokia 770 Internet Tablet, the first device runnin
events.text: Nokia announces the Nokia 770 Internet Tablet, the first device running Maemo.

events.title: AmigaOS 4 was released by Hyperion Entertainment (VOF) under license f
events.text: AmigaOS 4 was released by Hyperion Entertainment (VOF) under license from Amiga, Inc. for AmigaOne registered users.

events.title: Apple Computer introduces the MacBook Pro, their first Intel-based, du
events.text: Apple Computer introduces the MacBook Pro, their first Intel-based, dual-core mobile computer, as well as an Intel-based iMac.

events.title: Google announces acquisition of YouTube in $1
events.text: Google announces acquisition of YouTube in $1.65 billion deal, recognizing the growing importance of video content on the internet.

events.title: Intel announces plans for an 80-core processor that would exceed 1 TFL
events.text: Intel announces plans for an 80-core processor that would exceed 1 TFLOP, planned to be available in 2011.

events.title: Intel releases the Core 2 processor
events.text: Intel releases the Core 2 processor.

events.title: Intel releases the Core brand
events.text: Intel releases the Core brand. These are mobile 32-bit single-core and dual-core processors that were built using a modified design of the Pentium M's microarchitecture.

events.title: Nintendo releases the Wii
events.text: Nintendo releases the Wii.

events.text: Researchers create experimental processor that operates at higher than 500 GHz when cryogenically frozen.

events.text: Sony releases the PlayStation 3.

events.text: Twitter is launched, introducing a new platform for microblogging and social interaction.

events.text: AMD releases the Phenom line of high performance processors, positioning the Athlon as a mid-range line.

events.text: Apple launches Mac OS X Leopard (v10.5)

events.title: Asus announces the first Asus Eee PC, launching the netbook category o
events.text: Asus announces the first Asus Eee PC, launching the netbook category of mobile computers. It initially ran Linux; later models also offered a choice of Windows.

events.title: Microsoft Corporation launches Windows Vista more than 5 years after t
events.text: Microsoft Corporation launches Windows Vista more than 5 years after their last major, new operating system, Windows XP, was released.

events.title: The first iPhone was introduced by Apple
events.text: The first iPhone was introduced by Apple.

events.title: Blu-ray wins the high definition optical disc format war against HD DV
events.text: Blu-ray wins the high definition optical disc format war against HD DVD, becoming the industry standard for high-definition media.

events.title: The first public beta version of the Google Chrome web browser was rel
events.text: The first public beta version of the Google Chrome web browser was released. Chrome subsequently became the most popular web browser in the world, overtaking Internet Explorer.

events.title: The first version of Android was introduced by Google
events.text: The first version of Android was introduced by Google.

events.text: The HTC Dream (T-Mobile G1), the first commercially available device to run the Android operating system, was released.
